title: Purim: the feast and gifts
hook: two food gifts, gifts to two poor people, and a joyful meal
tomorrow: Saba says Passover cleaning means scrubbing the walls. does it?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Megillah: every word in order, noise for Haman, and a God who's never named. Hear it all. Then the scroll itself hands out the rest of the day's instructions.
screen: `HEAR IT ALL.` → `THE SCROLL HANDS OUT INSTRUCTIONS.`

segments.voice: Most parties come with a guest list. This one comes with a delivery list. The Book of Esther says the days are to be "days of feasting and gladness, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor." A feast, yes. But also food carried to friends, and gifts carried to strangers. Why would a day of joy send you out the door to people you may not even know?
screen: `A DELIVERY LIST.` → `FEASTING, PORTIONS, GIFTS TO THE POOR.` → `WHY SEND YOU OUT THE DOOR?`

segments.voice: The Talmud reads the plurals closely. Portions, one to another: at least two foods to one friend, called mishloach manot. Gifts to the poor: a gift each to at least two people in need. Then the meal, the seudah, later in the day. Maimonides weighs the three and comes down clearly. Better to spend more on gifts to the poor than on the feast or the portions, because there is no greater and more glorious joy than gladdening the hearts of the poor, the orphans, the widows and the strangers. So the joy of Purim travels outward: from the table, to a friend's door, to someone who has less. Now hold up the last six days together. Ordinary is holy too: Hillel's bath. Light in the window: lit for the street. Coins of light: some for play, some so another window glows. Fast with meaning: a meal's cost to the hungry. Plant something: Honi's carob. Hear it all: every word of the scroll. From a plain month to a feast, six lines.
screen: `TWO FOODS TO ONE FRIEND.` · `A GIFT EACH TO TWO IN NEED.` · `NO GREATER JOY.` · `SIX LINES, PLAIN MONTH TO FEAST.` · then, large: `GIFTS ON THE HAPPY DAY.`

segments.voice: For the sit, plan one food gift. Who gets it: a neighbor, a friend, someone who had a hard winter? What two things go in it: a piece of fruit, something baked, anything ready to eat? And one gift for someone in need, however small. Hold both faces in mind while the time runs.
screen: `WHO GETS IT?` · `TWO THINGS READY TO EAT.` · `ONE GIFT FOR SOMEONE IN NEED.`

segments.voice: Purim: the festival of Esther, kept with a feast, food to friends and gifts to the poor.
Your line: gifts on the happy day. The joy of Purim goes out the door to someone with less. Happy Purim.

howItsDone: On Purim day, Jews send mishloach manot, a gift of at least two ready-to-eat foods, to at least one friend, give gifts of money or food to at least two people in need, and hold a festive meal, the seudah, in the afternoon.
